question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$L=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $L-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
L-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(L-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(L-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-5\cdot 2 & =0 \\ -2+\lambda -2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 12}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{49}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm 7}{2} \\  & =-3,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4.$
